title: ⚑ Flagged for review — irregularities found while verifying, resolved or not
rule: a flag is published with the source links that expose it. Severity: high = a decision or a claim changes; medium = a number on the site can be wrong; low = hygiene. 'blocks' names what cannot be trusted until the flag is closed.

rows.title: 156 suggestion rows, 0 reviewer verdicts in git
rows.found: The census page counts every suggestion register in the repository and publishes the row, file and namespace totals from the pinned artefact; of those rows, only the number shown in the 'Rows w/ verdict' column carries a non-blank verdict-shaped field, and the page states why that is an upper bound. No file anywhere records a reviewer's verdict for the open queue — the field exists and is empty by design in every peer namespace too. If the pin is no longer reachable because the branch was rewritten, `python3 engine/inventory.py` reproduces the counts against whatever tree is checked out
rows.why_it_matters: the brief's process — review, choose a path, then implement — cannot be shown to have happened for any of them, so each new session re-proposes the same blockers.
rows.action: one verdict per row of CD-01…CD-15 in data/decisions.json (G-12); SF-02 makes a decided row visibly leave the queue
rows.blocks: any claim that the project has a decision process

rows.title: Third-party accounts of the inactive-list rule contradict each other
rows.found: Sources returned by search this session state 5, up to 7, and up to 8 inactives, and disagree on whether practice reports are due Mon–Wed or Wed–Fri. The only official artefact read prints 6 'Not Active' names per club for one fixture and states no rule.
rows.why_it_matters: a rule adopted from a non-official source would leak into capture schedules, denominators for 'who replaced whom', and any 'automatic inactive' assumption.
rows.action: reject all three numbers; measure the distribution of Not Active size across fixtures instead

rows.title: One fixture, two official venue names
rows.found: The game centre prints 'Location MUNICH / Stadium FC BAYERN MUNICH STADIUM'; the game book for the same fixture prints 'at Allianz Arena, Munich, Germany'.
rows.why_it_matters: a fixture-context join on venue name fails on international and neutral-site games, which are precisely the games where surface and conditions matter for a total.

rows.title: The game book carries a use restriction that no register records
rows.found: Its first page prints: media coverage only; 'any other use of this material is prohibited without the written permission of the National Football League'. Two peer namespaces transcribe from this document and one publishes lineup tables derived from it; a grep for the restriction's wording finds no register mentioning it.
rows.why_it_matters: the single best official source for starters, inactives, weather and venue comes with a condition printed on it, and the site's publication posture has never accounted for it.
rows.action: CD-03 (recommended: derived facts + a link, never a mirror); record the posture in the publication contract
rows.blocks: publishing transcribed game-book tables as such

rows.title: Two 'Out' players match no availability block, and two rows are ambiguous by surname
rows.found: engine/derive.py joins 24 report rows to the game book's four availability blocks for one fixture: 10 start, 5 come off the bench, 5 are Not Active, 2 match nothing (NE TreVeyon Henderson and DET Kerby Joseph, both 'Out' on the report) while the 'Did Not Play' block printed no names at all, and 2 rows are ambiguous because 'Brown' matches both 'A.Brown' in the lineups and 'B.Brown' in Not Active.
rows.why_it_matters: either the game book classifies an Out player in a way the site has not modelled, or the chunked renderer dropped the block - and no rendered read can tell those apart. Separately, the ambiguity shows the join cannot be keyed until an official name-to-number map exists, so 'who replaced whom' inherits that ceiling.
rows.action: CD-05: re-read the PDF's own text layer from bytes; if the block is genuinely empty, publish the classification gap as a fact about the artefact
rows.blocks: any 'every Out player is a Not Active' assumption and any play-rate denominator

rows.title: Game-day roster names in one game book sum to 54 per club
rows.found: For the fixture read, lineups (22 slots) plus substitutions (26) plus Not Active (6) enumerate 54 distinct names for each club, which exceeds a 53-man roster; the document does not state why (practice-squad elevations are a plausible route and are not printed here).
rows.why_it_matters: any model that assumes an active-count or roster-size constant will mis-handle exactly the games where elevations happen.
rows.action: do not adopt a constant; compare the count against the transactions hub for the same day before using it as a feature

rows.title: Every clock time in this repository is a client-side approximation
rows.found: The read path used by agent sessions returns rendered text only — no headers, no server Date, no bytes — so this namespace states its reads as an ordered window (01:31Z–01:36:08Z) rather than fake precision.
rows.why_it_matters: 'store every read with its clock time' and 'publish the delta' both promise a time series; what exists today is a set of agent notes with day-granularity.
rows.action: CD-04/G-04; until then, no page should print a timestamp finer than the window it was read in
rows.blocks: any claim about how fast a designation changed

rows.title: Two sibling CI gates are already red on main, and this namespace did not move them
rows.found: Reproduced on a clean checkout of `origin/main` on 2026-11-16 with nothing from this session applied, and byte-for-byte identical on this branch, so neither failure is caused by this PR. (1) `nfl-availability-desk verify` fails at its own 'Determinism gate (rebuild must not change committed files)': re-running that namespace's engine (capture -> audit -> drift -> build_site) rewrites five committed files (data/derived/capture_diffs.json, data/derived/hashes.json, pages/executive-summary.html, pages/repo-review.html, pages/snapshot-delta.html) because its cross-capture artefacts still describe a 107-row capture and '4 proper subsets' that the current tree no longer reproduces. (2) `Verify bounded NBA audit and published navigation` fails at 'Recompute HTML source-link and navigation coverage' because `verification-2026-11-05/index.html` publishes `../pages/competition.html`, which does not exist in that directory. This namespace's own job and the canonical-site job are both green.
rows.why_it_matters: every open pull request inherits two red checks that nothing in it caused, so 'CI is green' stops being usable as a merge signal; and the availability desk's cross-capture reconciliation numbers are now describing a tree that no longer exists
rows.action: owner of `nfl-availability-desk`: re-run the pipeline and commit the result, or pin the capture set to files under its own data/ so a sibling merge cannot move it. owner of `verification-2026-11-05`: the dead link is *generated* — line 131 of its `build.py` emits the tile `href="../pages/competition.html"`, and no `pages/competition.html` exists at the root any more, so either drop that tile and regenerate the snapshot or let the audit tolerate one documented removal. Both handed over in COORDINATION.md with the file and line; this PR edited neither namespace
rows.blocks: nothing this site publishes; it blocks a green board for the next session

rows.title: The first census page read an id collision as near-total duplication
rows.found: The clustering key is the row's title/question/item text, and two peer registers store only a row id there (`REQ-01`, `SUG-01`), so their rows cluster on the label. That put 68 rows in one 'requirement' cluster and 28 in one 'suggestion' cluster, and this page published those as the duplication finding. The engine now tells an identifier-keyed cluster from a shared sentence: the census page publishes both readings side by side, and the sentence columns are the finding — for requirements most rows with sentence text still sit inside a shared cluster, while for the peer suggestion rows only a small minority do (the exact counts are in the table's `Rows inside a duplicate sentence cluster` and `Largest sentence cluster` columns, computed from the pinned artefact rather than repeated here)
rows.why_it_matters: it inverts the finding. The open suggestion queue is barely duplicated, so the consolidation problem is the shared requirement text and the real gap is that no register records a verdict; a reviewer who acted on the inflated number would have spent the next session de-duplicating a backlog that was not duplicated
rows.action: closed in this commit: `engine/derive.py` flags identifier-keyed clusters, the census table carries both columns, the prose quotes the sentence numbers, and the raw figure stays visible and labelled
rows.blocks: nothing — the corrected numbers are the published ones

rows.title: This console attributed the n ≥ 300 gate to a file that does not contain it
rows.found: The landing page and QA-11 cited `nfl-availability-desk/data/governance.json` as the source of 'n ≥ 300 fixtures'. Re-read in full with the stderr no longer suppressed: that file is 8,040 bytes and contains the digits `300` zero times, and so does `nfl-book/data/gates.json` (3,586 bytes). The floor is real but is stated elsewhere and in a different unit — `nfl-command/data/gates.json` ('≥ 300 graded selections' for a strategy-level ROI claim), `nfl-arena/data/strategy_register.json` ('n >= 300 graded bets in the confirmatory window') and `nfl-availability-desk/prereg/PREREG-001-shadow-baseline.md` ('G1 sample | n ≥ 300 graded games'). No register states a fixture-level corpus floor.
rows.why_it_matters: the unit changes the conclusion. 'n ≥ 300 fixtures' makes one season provably too small and the leaderboard permanently closed; 'n ≥ 300 graded bets per strategy' is reachable inside a season for any strategy that settles more than about 1.1 bets per fixture. A reviewer deciding CD-06 on the first reading would have 'fixed' a problem that is actually an undefined unit, and left the real problem — no frozen counting rule — in place. It is also the exact failure mode this project exists to prevent: a number quoted with a confident file path nobody opened.
rows.action: closed in this commit for this namespace: `data/derived/corpus.json` now carries `unit_in_the_peer_wording`, `as_written_by_peers` (the three quoted lines with their files) and `mis_citation_corrected`; the landing row and QA-11 cite the three real files and say 'graded games per strategy'. Owners of `nfl-availability-desk` and `nfl-book` should check their own pages for the same phrasing — `nfl-availability-desk/engine/build_site.py` publishes 'a sample floor of n ≥ 300' with no unit, which is where this session inherited it
rows.blocks: nothing published after this commit; it blocks any promotion rule written before it

rows.title: Two peer registers store a serialized list in the field the census clusters on
rows.found: The census clusters on each row's title/question/item text. In `nfl-origination` and `nfl-price-snapshot` that field holds a whole Python-style list of dicts (a `[{"id": "S-01", ...}]` blob) rather than one sentence, so the clusterer sees one long unique string per row: those rows can only ever cluster with a byte-identical twin, which is how two of them ended up as a 2-row 'flag' cluster on the census page. The same field shape is why `rows with comparable text` is an upper bound for the flags and question kinds, and why their duplication counts are read as a floor.
rows.why_it_matters: a reviewer who reads '4 duplicated flag clusters' as 'the flag registers agree' is wrong in the comforting direction — schema drift, not agreement, is what keeps those counts low. Any cross-namespace deduplication has to normalize the row shape first, which is the same finding SF-01 makes about registers not agreeing on a schema
rows.action: the shared-register normalisation in CD-15 (one schema, one validator) is the fix; a temporary mitigation is already in place — the census publishes both the raw and the sentence-text columns, and this flag names the case the sentence columns cannot separate
rows.blocks: any claim that flag or question duplication across the repository is small
